purpose: Lock the parity direction: the standalone Atlas Mapper is a proving ground for the native Havenwild editor Asset Mapping Workspace and the later Ember editor workspace.
productLane: Havenwild native editor first, Ember ingest second
nativeEditorParityRules: The left asset area is a scrollable Source Atlas / Tile Sheet Stack loaded from the active Havenwild project asset lane.
The center surface is a real pannable game-world canvas using the same project worldgen, tile/layer model, and editor placement rules as Havenwild.
The right inspector edits semantic role, layer role, collision, sockets, adjacency, variants, and publish state for selected tiles, pieces, or world cells.
The tool rail controls edit modes: select, paint tile, replace tile, collision paint, socket paint, layer paint, erase, pan, sample, validate.
The layer rail exposes terrain_base, terrain_transition, terrain_overlay, terrain_detail, cliff_face, structure, object, collision, occlusion, actor/pathing, and debug overlays.
All mapping writes are metadata/recipe writes; source atlas pixels remain immutable.
Green tile checks mean mapping metadata exists for a source cell; sheet-level green means coverage rules pass; star/published means runtime authority promotion passed.

statusMeanings.tileDraft: source cell used in a correction scene, not yet certified
statusMeanings.tileMapped: source cell has role/layer/source rect mapping metadata
statusMeanings.tileValidated: source cell has required collision/socket/occlusion/animation metadata for its family
statusMeanings.sheetMapped: required cells for the sheet family meet coverage criteria
statusMeanings.published: runtime asset authority accepted the mapping
